quizName: DMV Practice Test #6 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: To control a motorcycle properly, you should:

options.text: Let your feet hang off the footrests.
Use your arms to hold up your body.
Keep your knees against the gas tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your knees against the gas tank.
questions.explanation: Keep your arms slightly bent and use them to steer, not to hold yourself up. Keep your knees against the gas tank to stay balanced, especially during turns.

questions.question: When choosing a protective jacket, it should:

options.text: Fit loosely and flap in the wind.
Fit snugly so it does not flap in the wind.
Not be made of leather or sturdy material.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fit snugly so it does not flap in the wind.
questions.explanation: Your jacket should be made of leather or another sturdy material. It should fit snugly enough to not flap in the wind, but loose enough to let you move freely.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should:
questions.explanation: When riding at night, slow down and stay farther behind other vehicles. Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to see the road better. Be ready to move lanes if needed.

questions.question: Which factor does not greatly affect your blood alcohol content (BAC)?
questions.explanation: Your BAC is mainly affected by how much alcohol you drink, how fast you drink it, and your body weight. Age does not play a major role.

questions.question: Oil drippings and debris usually collect in ______ of a lane.
questions.explanation: Oil drippings and debris from vehicles collect in the center of a lane.

questions.question: You see an emergency vehicle stopped on the side of the road with flashing lights. You should:

options.text: Stop on the road behind the emergency vehicle.
Stop and wait until the emergency vehicle moves.
Change lanes away from the emergency vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes away from the emergency vehicle.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle, tow truck, or roadside assistance vehicle with flashing lights, move to another lane to give it space. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: If your front wheel locks while braking, you should:

options.text: Keep the tire locked to stop faster.
Release the front brake and use only the rear brake.
Release the front brake and then re-apply it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake and then re-apply it.
questions.explanation: If the front wheel locks, release the front brake right away. Then apply pressure to the brake again, using steady, controlled pressure.

questions.question: Your motorcycle is weaving on bridge gratings. You should:

options.text: Keep a steady speed and ride straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a steady speed and ride straight.
questions.explanation: If your motorcycle weaves on bridge gratings, maintain a steady speed and go straight across. Do not swerve side to side.

questions.question: When it starts to rain, the best thing to do is:

options.text: Ride in the center of the lane.
Pull over and wait for the rain to stop.
Ride in the tire tracks left by other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Roads are slippery when rain first starts, especially in the center of the lane. Ride in the tire tracks left by other vehicles. The left tire track is usually the best choice.

questions.question: Service signs are:
questions.explanation: Blue signs with white letters show where services are located. These include rest areas, gas stations, food, and hospitals.

questions.question: When you prepare to pass a vehicle on the left, which part of your lane should you ride in?
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of your lane when you prepare to pass another vehicle on the left.

questions.question: When riding in a group, riders should generally be in:
questions.explanation: A staggered formation is best for group riding. It keeps riders close together while giving each rider enough space. Use single-file when taking curves, turning, or entering or leaving a highway.

questions.question: The best clothing for a motorcyclist:

options.text: Should not stand out to other motorists.

questions.explanation: Good riding clothes protect you in a crash. They should also keep you comfortable and make you visible to other drivers.

questions.question: When riding, your boots or shoes should:
questions.explanation: Wear boots or shoes that cover and support your ankles. Heels should be low so they don't catch on anything. Tuck in your shoelaces so they don't get caught on the motorcycle.

questions.question: To help others see your motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Keep eye contact with other drivers.

questions.explanation: Use your headlight to help other drivers see your motorcycle. Always check that your headlight works before you ride.

questions.question: As you drink more alcohol, your ability to safely ride:
questions.explanation: Your riding skills get worse as you drink more alcohol. Do not ride your motorcycle if you have consumed any alcohol.

questions.question: When riding behind a car in the left third of the lane, the driver can see you in their side mirror. What is a problem with this?

options.text: Most drivers don't check their side mirrors as often as their rearview mirror.
Wind can prevent the use of a side mirror.
Drivers should not use their side mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Most drivers don't check their side mirrors as often as their rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Most drivers look at their rearview mirror more often than their side mirrors. When following a car, ride in the center of the lane so the driver can see you in their rearview mirror.

questions.question: Taking a turn too fast can cause a rider to:

options.text: Cross into another lane of traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cross into another lane of traffic.
questions.explanation: Taking a turn too fast can cause you to cross into another lane or leave the road. Always slow down before entering a turn or curve.

questions.question: In the center of a traffic lane, there is usually an oily strip. Motorcyclists should:

options.text: Avoid riding on the oil and grease.
Not worry about the oil and grease.
Find the lane with the least oil and grease.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid riding on the oil and grease.
questions.explanation: Avoid the oily strip in the center of the lane. It is usually narrow enough that you can stay to the left or right of it and still be in the center portion of the lane.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you, which part of your lane should you be in?
questions.explanation: Stay in the center of your lane if a vehicle is passing you from behind or from the front. Don't move closer to the other driver, as this creates a hazard for both of you.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign is on the back of slow-moving vehicles that travel under 25 mph, such as farm equipment, construction machinery, or horse-drawn wagons.

questions.question: If a motorcyclist cannot avoid an obstacle on the road, they should:

options.text: Speed up before hitting the object.
Stay seated so the seat absorbs the impact.
Approach the obstacle at a 90-degree angle if possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Approach the obstacle at a 90-degree angle if possible.
questions.explanation: If you cannot avoid an obstacle, slow down and approach it at a 90-degree angle if you can. This is the safest way to ride over it.

questions.question: When riding during the day, you should wear:
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen in daylight. Wear clothing with reflective material to be more visible, even during the day. Always wear clothing that covers your arms and legs.

questions.question: For motorcycle riders, helmets are:
questions.explanation: In Georgia, you must wear a U.S. Department of Transportation-approved helmet whenever you operate a motorcycle.

questions.question: When traffic is slow or stopped, a motorcyclist should:

options.text: Not weave between lanes of traffic.
Weave in and out of traffic lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not weave between lanes of traffic.
questions.explanation: Riding between stopped or slow vehicles is dangerous. Other vehicles may change lanes, doors may open, or people may stick their arms out. Motorcycles need a full lane to operate safely.
